The 3-qubit GHZ circuit ran on the real sirius QPU with 100 shots. The job ID is 01a15f45-2000-7182-aa93-0702680e0436 and its status is completed. I first ran the same circuit once on the free sirius:mock as a check. That mock job ID is 01a15f44-f709-7750-8386-e0a57a1ac6c2, and it returned 000 on all 100 shots.

Counts from the real job, in Qiskit bit order: 000=51, 111=35, 001=3, 011=3, 100=3, 101=3, 110=2. The raw IQM counts list the first qubit on the left, so the mixed bitstrings appear in a different order there. The 000 and 111 counts are the same in both orders. 86 of the 100 shots were 000 or 111, so the GHZ fraction is 0.86.

Credits: the API did not report a credit amount for this job. The job record (GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}) has metrics.billed_seconds = 1.0, execution_seconds = 0.215, and runtime_seconds = 0.283. It has no cost or credit field. The runtime_estimates artifact and the quantum-computers list also have no credit field. For that reason I set credits_reported to 0. The IQM Academy rate for sirius is 0.3 credits per second, which would make 1 billed second about 0.3 credits. That figure is an estimate from the docs and the API did not report it. The dashboard Jobs view shows the actual billed cost.

The scripts are run_ghz.py and check_art.py in /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_f3caa17a-2c4-286/. The saved job records are jobrecord_sirius.json and jobrecord_sirius_mock.json in the same folder.
